method: Callgrind Ir counts executed instructions, not hardware CPU cycles or elapsed-time shares. Exclusive function counts reconcile with the profiler total; inclusive edge costs overlap. DHAT replaces allocator routines and records requested heap bytes, blocks, and lifetimes by allocation stack; these bytes are allocation traffic, not RSS. Instrumented elapsed times are excluded from performance comparisons.
verification: All manifests, preserved binaries, frozen build snapshots, inputs and full stdout rechecked; raw traces reparsed with the shared driver and reconciled with stored summaries. No measured program was executed.

attribution_notes: Stages are cumulative development snapshots; dirty revisions are identified by exact frozen source/build hashes, not by the commit ID alone.

Storage and flags have byte-identical .text sections and equal allocation/peak metrics. Flags has 14 additional whole-process instructions per workload, all attributed to the same external address-named function; this is not an nsw benefit. No generated-code improvement is established by this stage or its timing differences.
The first locals profile failed because an objcopy inspection rewrote its binary during profiling. It is excluded. Only the completed dependency-index-locals-profile-restored retry is accepted.

Inspection also changed storage/flags/locals/cold ELF metadata after their measurements. Preserved binaries are accepted only when restored whole-file hashes exactly equal the original comparison and completed profile records.
Callgrind instruction counts and exclusive function fractions are not wall-time shares. Inlining changes function attribution. DHAT allocation/peak bytes are not process RSS.
The reused Rust references preserve the same algorithm; checked-i64 has a narrower numeric domain than Relar and Rust BigInt. These two captured workloads fit that domain.
Raw traces, logs, outputs and source snapshots remain in ignored local evidence directories; this compact record stores hashes and summaries instead of source contents.
